args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and review why an unhealthy staging RC was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001. The service is healthy again.

- **The problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west and failing health checks, with an 18% error rate. The test build for v2.3.1 had also failed health checks in staging but was still released to production.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the last release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production, this didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open and has paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure and the rollback. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure should be found before it's deployed again, and asks why it went to production after failing in staging.
